prerequisites: Successful participation in the Theoretical Computer Science module from the Bachelor's degree program in Computer Science.

learning_outcomes.text: Students can classify problems according to their computational difficulty.
Students can compare different classes of problems with each other.
Students can compare the computational power of different machine models, such as randomized and non-deterministic Turing machines.

syllabus_topics: Complexity classes, such as LOGSPACE, P, NP, PSPACE

assessment_methods.method: Oral examination (individual examination) or written exam

assessment_rules: Grading is done with 0 to 15 points according to the examination regulations for the M.Sc. Computer Science degree program.
bibliography: Sanjeev Arora, Boaz Barak: Computational Complexity - A Modern Approach. Cambridge University Press 2009
Christos H. Papadimitriou: Computational complexity. Academic Internet Publ. 2007
Ingo Wegener: Complexity theory - exploring the limits of efficient algorithms. Springer 2005
Rodney G. Downey, Michael R. Fellows: Fundamentals of Parameterized Complexity. Texts in Computer Science, Springer 2013
